\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مسرحية} (masraḥiyya)}{مسرحية (masraḥiyya)}]{\ar{مسرحية} (masraḥiyya) — a stage play}

\label{lesson:AR-C542-masrahiyya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to carve, then the Arabic for a painter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مسرحية}}
\textbf{\ar{مسرحية}} — \emph{masraḥiyya} — \textquotedblleft{}a stage play\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{شاهدنا} \ar{مسرحية} \ar{مضحكة} \ar{في} \ar{المسرح}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shāhadnā masraḥiyya muḍḥika fī al-masraḥ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We watched a funny play at the theatre.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مسرحية}} (\emph{masraḥiyya}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-r-ḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}to send out to pasture\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Masraḥ, a theatre, which you know, first named a pasture: a wide open place.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{masraḥiyya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{masraḥiyya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shāhadnā masraḥiyya muḍḥika fī al-masraḥ.} — We watched a funny play at the theatre.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to carve, then the Arabic for a painter, then say \emph{masraḥiyya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مسرحية} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A stage play\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مشهد} (mashhad)}{مشهد (mashhad)}]{\ar{مشهد} (mashhad) — a scene; a view}

\label{lesson:AR-C542-mashhad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a painter, then the Arabic for a stage play.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مشهد}}
\textbf{\ar{مشهد}} — \emph{mashhad} — \textquotedblleft{}a scene; a view\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{بكت} \ar{أختي} \ar{في} \ar{المشهد} \ar{الأخير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bakat ukhtī fī al-mashhad al-akhīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister cried at the last scene.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{مشاهد}, \emph{mashāhid}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مشهد}} (\emph{mashhad}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{sh-h-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to be present, to witness\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Shāhada, to watch, which you know, is from the same root: a mashhad is what is witnessed.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mashhad}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mashhad}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bakat ukhtī fī al-mashhad al-akhīr.} — My sister cried at the last scene.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a painter, then the Arabic for a stage play, then say \emph{mashhad} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مشهد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A scene; a view\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تصفيق} (taṣfīq)}{تصفيق (taṣfīq)}]{\ar{تصفيق} (taṣfīq) — applause}

\label{lesson:AR-C542-tasfiq}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a stage play, then the Arabic for a scene.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تصفيق}}
\textbf{\ar{تصفيق}} — \emph{taṣfīq} — \textquotedblleft{}applause\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{سمعنا} \ar{تصفيقا} \ar{طويلا} \ar{بعد} \ar{الأغنية}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{samiʿnā taṣfīqan ṭawīlan baʿda al-ughniya.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We heard long applause after the song.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تصفيق}} (\emph{taṣfīq}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṣ-f-q}, \textquotedblleft{}to strike, to clap\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Taṣfīq is the verbal noun of Form II.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taṣfīq}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taṣfīq}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{samiʿnā taṣfīqan ṭawīlan baʿda al-ughniya.} — We heard long applause after the song.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a stage play, then the Arabic for a scene, then say \emph{taṣfīq} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تصفيق} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Applause\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{صفق} (ṣaffaqa)}{صفق (ṣaffaqa)}]{\ar{صفق} (ṣaffaqa) — to applaud}

\label{lesson:AR-C542-saffaqa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a scene, then the Arabic for applause.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{صفق}}
\textbf{\ar{صفق}} — \emph{ṣaffaqa} — \textquotedblleft{}to applaud\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{صفق} \ar{الناس} \ar{للممثلين}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ṣaffaqa an-nās li-l-mumaththilīn.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The people applauded the actors.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يصفق}, \emph{yuṣaffiq}.

It takes \ar{لـ} for the one applauded.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{صفق}} (\emph{ṣaffaqa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṣ-f-q}, \textquotedblleft{}to strike, to clap\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Form II ṣaffaqa is to clap again and again.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣaffaqa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣaffaqa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣaffaqa an-nās li-l-mumaththilīn.} — The people applauded the actors.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a scene, then the Arabic for applause, then say \emph{ṣaffaqa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{صفق} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To applaud\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تمثيل} (tamthīl)}{تمثيل (tamthīl)}]{\ar{تمثيل} (tamthīl) — acting}

\label{lesson:AR-C542-tamthil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for applause, then the Arabic for to applaud.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تمثيل}}
\textbf{\ar{تمثيل}} — \emph{tamthīl} — \textquotedblleft{}acting\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{درست} \ar{أختي} \ar{التمثيل} \ar{في} \ar{الجامعة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{darasat ukhtī at-tamthīl fī al-jāmiʿa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister studied acting at university.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تمثيل}} (\emph{tamthīl}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{m-th-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to be like, to resemble\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Mumaththil, an actor, which you know, is from the same root: acting is making a likeness.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tamthīl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{darasat ukhtī at-tamthīl fī al-jāmiʿa.} — My sister studied acting at university.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for applause, then the Arabic for to applaud, then say \emph{tamthīl} again
\end{itemize}
